findings.title: llms.txt index hygiene: duplicate URLs and entries without a description
findings.agentImpact: An agent picking pages from llms.txt uses the one-line description to decide what to fetch. Entries without one are opaque; duplicates waste retrieval budget.

evidence.note: line 196: no description ("KYC action required snapshot report")

findings.recommendation: Generate llms.txt from the same source of truth as the page frontmatter so every entry carries `description`, and dedupe on canonical URL.

findings.title: llms.txt and sitemap.xml disagree on which pages exist
findings.agentImpact: Two machine-readable indexes of the same site disagree. An agent that trusts llms.txt never sees pages only the sitemap lists, and vice versa.
findings.recommendation: Emit both files from one page manifest in the docs build and add a CI assertion that the two URL sets are equal.

findings.title: llms.txt links that do not return a 200 Markdown document
findings.agentImpact: A link in llms.txt is a promise that the page exists as Markdown. Every broken or HTML-returning link is an agent fetch that fails or feeds HTML into a Markdown parser.
findings.recommendation: Run this link check in the docs CI on every deploy; fail the build on any non-200 or non-Markdown response for a URL that llms.txt advertises.

findings.title: docs.adyen.com answers a plain HTTP client with a Cloudflare JavaScript challenge (HTTP 429, cf-mitigated: challenge) after about 1,002 Markdown fetches
findings.agentImpact: robots.txt invites AI agents in and llms.txt hands them 2,500 Markdown URLs, but the edge serves a browser-only challenge page once a client reads the corpus at any speed. An agent cannot execute the challenge, receives an HTML body on a .md URL, and gets no Retry-After to plan around. The tooling says 'crawl me'; the CDN says 'prove you are a browser'.

evidence.note: HTTP 429, content-type text/html, cf-mitigated: challenge, no Retry-After (single request, identifying User-Agent)
run 1: 1002 pages OK then 1523 challenge pages at concurrency 12 in 22s

findings.recommendation: Exempt `/*.md`, `/llms.txt` and `/llms-full.txt` from managed challenges (or key the rate limit on the identifying User-Agent and return a real 429 with Retry-After), and publish the crawl budget in llms.txt.

findings.title: llms-full.txt is 51.1 MB (about 13.4M tokens), larger than any model context
findings.agentImpact: llms-full.txt exists so an agent can load the whole corpus in one read. At this size no current model can, so agents that follow the llms.txt pointer either fail the fetch or truncate silently and reason from the first few hundred pages (the Account and Customer Area sections).

evidence.note: line 5 points agents at llms-full.txt as 'the full concatenated Markdown corpus of every page'

findings.recommendation: Split llms-full.txt per product section (Online payments, Platforms, Issuing, POS, Risk) and per language track, each under ~2M tokens; keep the aggregate file but add its size to the llms.txt line so agents can plan.

findings.title: 6 pages exceed 100k tokens each because every language tab is inlined
findings.agentImpact: The .md rendering flattens every code-language tab into one document. An agent asking for the Node.js sessions flow receives Java, Kotlin, Swift, PHP, Go, C#, Ruby and Python as well, and may not fit the page in context at all.
findings.recommendation: Honour a `?lang=` query (or `Accept-Language`-style header) on .md URLs, or publish one .md per language tab and list them in llms.txt.

findings.title: 270 of 19,084 code fences carry no language tag
findings.agentImpact: A fence without a language is untyped text to an agent: it cannot tell a JSON request body from a shell command from a webhook payload, cannot lint it, and cannot choose it when the user asked for a specific language.

evidence.note: odd number of ``` fences (block never closes)

findings.recommendation: Add a docs lint rule: every fence has a language; treat `json`, `bash`, and `text` as the fallbacks.

findings.title: 847 of 7,870 JSON/JS/TS/Python snippets do not parse, even as fragments; 526 more parse only after dedenting or wrapping
findings.agentImpact: Agents copy snippets verbatim. A JSON example with `...` or a comment fails JSON.parse in the agent's own tool call; a JS block that does not parse is a broken first attempt the agent must debug before it can help the developer.
findings.recommendation: Lint every fenced snippet in CI (JSON.parse, tsc parse diagnostics, python ast). Replace `...` with a complete minimal example or move the elision into a comment outside the fence; strip list indentation from fenced blocks in the Markdown renderer.

findings.title: Docs-template markup ({hint:...}{/hint}) leaks into 115 Markdown pages, 66 times inside JSON examples
findings.agentImpact: The HTML renderer turns {hint:...} into a tooltip; the Markdown renderer prints it verbatim, so a JSON example contains "{hint:This is the card alias}M4695...{/hint}" where a value should be. An agent that copies it ships the markup, and JSON.parse still succeeds because it sits inside a string, so nothing catches it downstream.
findings.recommendation: Strip or resolve {hint:} in the Markdown export (render the hint as a trailing comment outside the fence) and add a grep for `{hint:` to the docs CI.

findings.title: 245 pages mix Checkout API versions in their own examples; 67 never mention the current v72
findings.agentImpact: The OpenAPI spec and the Node SDK are at Checkout v72. Docs examples still call older versions, sometimes three different ones on the same page. An agent has no way to know which is current and will pin a new integration to whatever it read first.
findings.recommendation: Template the version into snippets from one constant (`{{checkoutVersion}}`) and bump it in one commit when the spec releases; assert in CI that no page contains more than one version.

findings.title: 120 API Explorer links pin an older Checkout version; 0 point at paths absent from the v72 spec
findings.agentImpact: API Explorer links are the docs' own pointer into the reference. Links pinned to an older version send an agent to a reference that disagrees with the SDK; links to missing paths send it nowhere.
findings.recommendation: Link to `/api-explorer/Checkout/latest/...` everywhere and validate each explorer link against the published spec in CI.

findings.title: 8 of 40 JSON request examples use fields the v72 spec does not define; 9 omit a required field
findings.agentImpact: Agents validate their tool calls against the OpenAPI schema (the official MCP server is generated from it). A docs example with a field the schema lacks either gets rejected client-side or teaches the agent a field that the API ignores. A required field missing from the example is a guaranteed 422 on the first try.

findings.title: 801 of 2523 pages declare a last_modified more than 3 years old (456 more than 5)
findings.agentImpact: The posting's own words: stale content misleads agents as much as people. The .md frontmatter exposes `last_modified`, which is the right signal, but it is either very old or absent on a large share of pages, so an agent cannot down-weight stale guidance.
findings.recommendation: Set `last_modified` from git history on every page, expose the same value as the HTTP Last-Modified header, and add a `reviewed_on` field so agents can distinguish 'old but verified' from 'old'.

findings.title: 57,539 links in the .md corpus are site-relative; 396 distinct targets are not in llms.txt
findings.agentImpact: A .md page fetched by URL contains links like `/payment-methods`. An agent must guess the host and append `.md` to follow them; when the target is not in llms.txt the guess fails. Absolute `.md` links would let an agent walk the corpus without heuristics.

findings.title: llms.txt lists 0 API reference pages; the guides link to the API Explorer 11,370 times
findings.agentImpact: The guides defer field-level detail to the API Explorer, which is a JavaScript application with no Markdown rendering and no llms.txt entry. An agent reading the corpus can reach the prose but not the schema it is told to consult, so it guesses field names.

evidence.note: CheckoutService-v72.json has 29 operations, none exposed as Markdown

findings.recommendation: Render one Markdown page per operation from the OpenAPI spec (this repo's `data/llms-checkout.txt` is a generated example) and list them in a `## API reference` section of llms.txt.

findings.title: Official @adyen/mcp covers 8 of 29 Checkout operations; POST /payments and /payments/details are not among them
findings.agentImpact: An agent with the official server can create a session or a payment link but cannot run the Advanced flow (/payments, /payments/details) or check a test card, which is what most integration debugging needs. Its README also pins Checkout v71 while the spec and SDK are at v72.

evidence.note: tool list parsed on 2026-09-15: 40 operations across Checkout and Management

findings.recommendation: Generate the tool list from the OpenAPI spec so coverage and version move together; this repo's MCP adds /payments, /payments/details and a test-card catalogue for the TEST environment.

findings.title: robots.txt explicitly allows 6 named AI crawlers and publishes llms.txt: the posture is right, the content is the gap
findings.agentImpact: Agents are welcome at the door. Every finding above is about what they find once inside.

evidence.note: Allow: / for GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended, CCBot, anthropic-ai
present; every page also served as Markdown via `.md`

findings.recommendation: Keep it. Add `Sitemap:` and `llms.txt` hints to the HTML `<head>` (`<link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown">`) so agents that land on an HTML page discover the Markdown twin.
